at efterkomme.explanation: "At efterkomme" means "to comply with", to do what a request, a rule or an order asks: Hun efterkom min anmodning (She met my request).

sentence.da: Man skal **efterkomme** en ordre fra politiet.
sentence.en: You must comply with an order from the police.

at efterlade.explanation: "At efterlade" means "to leave behind": something stays when you go. Du kan efterlade en besked (You can leave a message). Do not mix it up with at forlade (to leave a place or a person for good).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **efterlade** skrald i skoven.
sentence.en: You must not leave trash behind in the forest.

at efterligne.explanation: "At efterligne" means "to imitate", to do what someone does or to sound like them: Børn efterligner de voksne (Children imitate adults). It is also used for fakes: Tasken er en efterligning af en dyr taske (The bag is a copy of an expensive bag).

sentence.da: Papegøjer kan **efterligne** menneskers stemme.
sentence.en: Parrots can imitate people's voices.

at efterlyse.explanation: "At efterlyse" means "to call for" or "to search for". The police use it to ask the public for help finding a missing person, a car or witnesses: Politiet efterlyser vidner (The police are appealing for witnesses). It is also used for saying something is missing and needed: Vi efterlyser flere penge til skolen (We are calling for more money for the school).

forms.en: I have called for / searched for

sentence.da: Familien vil **efterlyse** sin forsvundne kat på sociale medier.
sentence.en: The family wants to appeal for their missing cat on social media.

at efterspørge.explanation: "At efterspørge" means "to demand" or "to ask for". It is used for a market where customers want a product: Folk efterspørger flere cykelstier (People are asking for more bike lanes). Unlike at kræve (to insist), it is only about wanting something.

sentence.da: Flere kunder begynder at **efterspørge** økologiske varer.
sentence.en: More customers are starting to ask for organic goods.

at eje.explanation: "At eje" means "to own": Han ejer to huse (He owns two houses). In everyday talk, Danes often just say at have (to have): Jeg har en bil (I have a car).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **eje** sit eget hus.
sentence.en: He would like to own his own house.

at eksistere.explanation: "At eksistere" means "to exist": Dinosaurer eksisterer ikke længere (Dinosaurs no longer exist). In everyday talk, Danes often say findes (exist) instead: Findes der en bus? (Is there a bus?)

sentence.da: Drager kan ikke **eksistere** i virkeligheden.
sentence.en: Dragons cannot exist in real life.

at eksperimentere.explanation: "At eksperimentere" means "to experiment", to try something new to see what happens, in science and in daily life. The little word med (with) names what you try: Vi eksperimenterer med nye opskrifter (We are experimenting with new recipes).

sentence.da: I fysiktimen må vi **eksperimentere** med strøm og magneter.
sentence.en: In physics class we get to experiment with electricity and magnets.

at eksplodere.explanation: "At eksplodere" means "to explode": Bomben eksploderede (The bomb exploded). It also works for feelings: Han eksploderede af vrede (He exploded with anger).

sentence.da: Flasken kan **eksplodere**, når den bliver for varm.
sentence.en: The bottle can explode when it gets too hot.

at eksportere.explanation: "At eksportere" means "to export", to sell goods to other countries: Danmark eksporterer svinekød (Denmark exports pork). It is also used on a computer: at eksportere en fil (to export a file).

sentence.da: Landet vil **eksportere** mere fisk til udlandet.
sentence.en: The country wants to export more fish abroad.

at elske.explanation: "At elske" means "to love". It is a strong word, kept mostly for people you truly care about: Jeg elsker dig (I love you). For food and things, it is a playful exaggeration: Jeg elsker pizza (I love pizza).

sentence.da: Hun vil **elske** sine børn for evigt.
sentence.en: She will love her children forever.

at ende.explanation: "At ende" means "to end" and also "to end up": Historien endte godt (The story ended well). Vi endte i Aarhus (We ended up in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, at filmen vil **ende** godt.
sentence.en: I think the movie will end well.

at ende med.explanation: "At ende med" means "to end up with" something, or "to end up doing" something: Jeg endte med en forkølelse (I ended up with a cold). Han endte med at købe en cykel (He ended up buying a bike).

sentence.da: Vi vil nok **ende med** at blive hjemme.
sentence.en: We will probably end up staying at home.

at enes.explanation: "At enes" means "to agree", to reach the same view together, and also "to get along". It needs two or more people, so it goes with vi (we) or de (they): Vi enedes om prisen (We agreed on the price). In the negative it often means not getting along: De kan ikke enes (They cannot get along).

sentence.da: Mine to brødre kan aldrig **enes** om noget.
sentence.en: My two brothers can never agree on anything.

at engagere sig.explanation: "At engagere sig" means "to get involved", to join in actively in something you care about. It is usually followed by i (in): Hun engagerer sig i den lokale idrætsklub (She gets involved in the local sports club).

sentence.da: Mange unge vil **engagere sig**, fordi de bekymrer sig om klimaet.
sentence.en: Many young people want to get involved because they worry about the climate.

at erfare.explanation: "At erfare" means "to find out" and "to experience", to learn something from your own experience: Jeg har erfaret, at toget ofte er forsinket (I have found out that the train is often late).

sentence.da: Man kan kun **erfare** det ved selv at prøve.
sentence.en: You can only find it out by trying it yourself.

at erklære.explanation: "At erklære" means "to declare", to say something clearly and with weight, often officially: Landet erklærer krig (The country declares war). It is also used for feelings and opinions: at erklære sin kærlighed (to declare your love).

sentence.da: Hun vil **erklære**, at hun stopper som formand.
sentence.en: She will declare that she is stepping down as chair.

at erobre.explanation: "At erobre" means "to conquer", to take a country or a city by force. It also works for winning people or a market: at erobre markedet (to conquer the market).

sentence.da: Hæren vil **erobre** byen med magt.
sentence.en: The army wants to conquer the city by force.

at erstatte.explanation: "At erstatte" means "to replace", to put one thing in the place of another. It also means paying someone back for a loss: at erstatte en skade (to pay back for damage).

sentence.da: Forsikringen vil **erstatte** den ødelagte telefon med en ny.
sentence.en: The insurance will replace the broken phone with a new one.

at etablere.explanation: "At etablere" means "to establish", to set something up so that it lasts: a company, a system or a contact. With sig (oneself) it means to get settled somewhere: Hun har etableret sig som tandlæge (She has set herself up as a dentist).

sentence.da: De vil **etablere** et nyt firma i København.
sentence.en: They want to establish a new company in Copenhagen.

at evakuere.explanation: "At evakuere" means "to evacuate", to get people out of a dangerous place such as a burning building or a flooded area. You can name the people or the place: at evakuere skolen (to evacuate the school).

sentence.da: Politiet må **evakuere** huset, fordi der er brand.
sentence.en: The police must evacuate the house because there is a fire.

at evaluere.explanation: "At evaluere" means "to evaluate", to look back at how something went and judge it. It is common after a project, a course or a school year: Vi evaluerer kurset sammen (We evaluate the course together).

sentence.da: Efter projektet skal vi **evaluere**, hvad der gik godt.
sentence.en: After the project, we must evaluate what went well.

e-boks.explanation: "En e-Boks" means "an e-Boks", the digital mailbox where public offices, banks and companies send you letters.

forms.da: Jeg har et brev i e-Boks.
forms.en: I have a letter in e-Boks.

sentence.da: Jeg har fået et brev i **e-Boks**.
sentence.en: I have received a letter in e-Boks.

eddike.explanation: "Eddike" means "vinegar", the liquid with a sharp taste used in salad dressing and for pickling vegetables.

sentence.da: Salaten smager surt, fordi der er **eddike** i.
sentence.en: The salad tastes sour because there is vinegar in it.

effektiv.explanation: "Effektiv" means "efficient" for a person or method that gets things done without wasting time, and "effective" for something that works well: Medicinen er effektiv (The medicine is effective).

sentence.da: Han er meget **effektiv** og bliver hurtigt færdig.
sentence.en: He is very efficient and finishes quickly.

efter.explanation: "Efter" means "after". In some phrases, it means "for": at lede efter nøglerne (to look for the keys). Before a whole sentence, say efter at: efter at jeg kom hjem (after I came home).

sentence.da: Vi går en tur **efter** middagen.
sentence.en: We go for a walk after dinner.

efter min mening.explanation: "Efter min mening" means "in my opinion" and introduces what you think. The word er (is) comes right after it, before what you are talking about: Efter min mening er filmen for lang (In my opinion the movie is too long).

sentence.da: **Efter min mening** er suppen for salt.
sentence.en: In my opinion the soup is too salty.

efterfølgende.explanation: "Efterfølgende" means "subsequently", for something that happens after what you just mentioned. Before a word it means "following": den efterfølgende dag (the following day).

sentence.da: Vi ses til mødet og spiser **efterfølgende** sammen.
sentence.en: We will see each other at the meeting and eat together afterwards.

efterhånden.explanation: "Efterhånden" means "gradually", a bit at a time as time passes. It also means "by now", when something has been building up: Jeg er efterhånden træt af det (I am getting tired of it by now).

forms.en: I am learning it step by step
It is getting late by now

sentence.da: Det bliver **efterhånden** koldere, når efteråret kommer.
sentence.en: It gradually gets colder when fall comes.

efterhånden som.explanation: "Efterhånden som" means "as", for a change that builds up step by step while something else goes on. Mens (while) only says that two things happen at the same time, but efterhånden som adds that it grows over time.

sentence.da: **Efterhånden som** børnene vokser, får de flere pligter.
sentence.en: As the children grow, they get more duties.

efterlyst.explanation: "Efterlyst" means "wanted", said of a person or thing that the police publicly ask people to help find. Eftersøgt (sought) only says that someone is looking, with no appeal to everyone.

related.en: to put out a call for

sentence.da: Manden er **efterlyst**, og politiet beder folk om hjælp.
sentence.en: The man is wanted, and the police ask people for help.

eftersom.explanation: "Eftersom" means "since" or "because", and gives a reason that the listener already knows or can see. For a reason that answers the question why, use fordi (because).

forms.da: Eftersom du er her, kan vi begynde
forms.en: Since you are here, we can begin

forms.da: Eftersom han er syg, kommer han ikke
forms.en: Since he is sick, he is not coming

forms.da: Vi bliver hjemme, eftersom det regner
forms.en: We are staying home since it is raining

sentence.da: **Eftersom** det er sent, tager jeg hjem.
sentence.en: Since it is late, I am going home.

efterspørgsel.explanation: "En efterspørgsel" means "demand", how much people want to buy or get something. The thing wanted comes after på: efterspørgsel på billige boliger (demand for cheap homes).

sentence.da: Når der er stor **efterspørgsel**, stiger priserne ofte.
sentence.en: When there is great demand, prices often go up.

eftersøgt.explanation: "Eftersøgt" means "wanted" or "sought", for someone or something that people are looking for. It can also mean that many people want it: en eftersøgt ekspert (an expert many people want to hire). Efterlyst is the version where the police publicly ask for help.

sentence.da: Hunden har været **eftersøgt** i flere dage, men ingen har set den.
sentence.en: The dog has been searched for several days, but no one has seen it.

eftertragtet.explanation: "Eftertragtet" means "sought-after", something many people want and compete for: en eftertragtet uddannelse (a sought-after education). It always says the thing is valuable.

sentence.da: En lejlighed i centrum er **eftertragtet**, og der er lang venteliste.
sentence.en: An apartment downtown is sought-after, and there is a long waiting list.

egen.explanation: "Egen" means "own", and it goes with words like min (my) or din (your): mit eget værelse (my own room), mine egne ting (my own things).

sentence.da: Jeg har min **egen** bil.
sentence.en: I have my own car.

egentlig.explanation: "Egentlig" means "actually" or "really", and often hints at a plan that changed: Jeg skulle egentlig arbejde (I was actually supposed to work). In questions it asks what is really true: Hvad vil du egentlig? (What do you really want?).

sentence.da: Jeg ville **egentlig** gå hjem, men jeg blev.
sentence.en: I actually wanted to go home, but I stayed.

egnet.explanation: "Egnet" means "suitable", right for a certain purpose or person. The purpose usually comes after til (for): Filmen er egnet til børn (The film is suitable for children).

sentence.da: Skoen er **egnet** til at løbe i.
sentence.en: The shoe is suitable for running in.

egoistisk.explanation: "Egoistisk" means "selfish" and describes someone who thinks only of themselves. The opposite is uselvisk (unselfish).

sentence.da: Han er **egoistisk** og tænker kun på sig selv.
sentence.en: He is selfish and only thinks of himself.

ejendele.explanation: "Ejendele" means "belongings", the things that belong to a person. One item is en ejendel (a belonging), but the plural is what you usually see. Do not mix it up with en ejendom (a property), which is land or a building.

sentence.da: Tøj, bøger og min telefon er mine **ejendele**.
sentence.en: Clothes, books and my phone are my belongings.

ejendommelig.explanation: "Ejendommelig" means "peculiar", odd or unusual in a way that you notice. It can also mean typical of something: Dialekten er ejendommelig for egnen (The dialect is characteristic of the area).

sentence.da: Der var en **ejendommelig** stilhed i rummet, da han kom ind.
sentence.en: There was a peculiar silence in the room when he came in.

eksisterende.explanation: "Eksisterende" means "existing", already there, as opposed to something new. It comes from at eksistere (to exist) and is often paired with ny (new): nye og eksisterende kunder (new and existing customers).

sentence.da: Vi vil bygge videre på det **eksisterende** system.
sentence.en: We want to build on the existing system.

eksklusiv.explanation: "Eksklusiv" means "exclusive", special and meant for few people, often with a high price. In prices it means "not included": 100 kr. eksklusiv moms (100 kr. without VAT).

sentence.da: Det er en **eksklusiv** klub, kun for medlemmer.
sentence.en: It is an exclusive club, only for members.

eksport.explanation: "En eksport" means "an export", goods that go to buyers in other countries, and also the act of sending them. What is sent comes after af: eksport af maskiner (export of machines).

sentence.da: Mange danske firmaer lever af **eksport** til udlandet.
sentence.en: Many Danish firms live off exports to other countries.

ekstra.explanation: "Ekstra" means "extra", more than you already have: en ekstra stol (an extra chair). Before another word, it makes that word stronger: ekstra stor (extra large), ekstra god (extra good).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en **ekstra** stol, tak.
sentence.en: We need an extra chair, please.

ekstraordinær.explanation: "Ekstraordinær" means "extraordinary", either very impressive or simply outside the normal routine: en ekstraordinær generalforsamling (an extraordinary general meeting, held outside the normal schedule).

sentence.da: Hun har gjort en **ekstraordinær** indsats for holdet.
sentence.en: She has made an extraordinary effort for the team.

ekstrem.explanation: "Ekstrem" means "extreme", at the very edge of what is normal, for weather, temperatures, sports and opinions.

sentence.da: Der er **ekstrem** varme i ørkenen om sommeren.
sentence.en: There is extreme heat in the desert in summer.

ekstremt.explanation: "Ekstremt" means "extremely". It goes before another word and is stronger than meget (very).

sentence.da: I dag er det **ekstremt** varmt.
sentence.en: Today it is extremely hot.

elegant.explanation: "Elegant" means "elegant", nice to look at in a simple, well-made way. It is used for clothes, movements and places, and also for a clever solution: en elegant løsning (an elegant solution).

sentence.da: En **elegant** kjole er enkel, men flot syet.
sentence.en: An elegant dress is simple but beautifully sewn.

elektricitet.explanation: "Elektricitet" means "electricity". In daily life, Danes often say strøm (power): Strømmen er gået (The power is out).

sentence.da: Uden **elektricitet** virker lyset og computeren ikke.
sentence.en: Without electricity the light and the computer do not work.

elektrisk.explanation: "Elektrisk" means "electric", for things that run on power instead of fuel or muscle. Danes say strøm (power) for the power itself: Der er ingen strøm (There is no power).

sentence.da: Min bil er **elektrisk** og kører uden benzin.
sentence.en: My car is electric and runs without gasoline.

elektronik.explanation: "Elektronik" means "electronics", the devices and parts that work with small chips and screens. For one device, say en enhed (a device).

sentence.da: Butikken sælger **elektronik** som telefoner og computere.
sentence.en: The store sells electronics such as phones and computers.

elendig.explanation: "Elendig" means "miserable" or "terrible": Jeg har det elendigt (I feel terrible). It also describes very poor quality: Han er en elendig sanger (He is a terrible singer).

sentence.da: Den gamle bil er **elendig**, og den starter aldrig.
sentence.en: The old car is terrible, and it never starts.

eller.explanation: "Eller" means "or": te eller kaffe? (tea or coffee?). Added at the end of a question, it asks for agreement, like right?: Du kommer, eller? (You are coming, right?). Don't mix it up with ellers (otherwise): Skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent (Hurry up, or we will be late).

sentence.da: Vil du have te **eller** kaffe?
sentence.en: Do you want tea or coffee?

ellers.explanation: "Ellers" means "otherwise" or "or else", and it names what happens if something is not done. It also means "else" in questions: Hvad ellers? (What else?). Don't mix it up with eller (or): te eller kaffe (tea or coffee).

forms.da: skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent
forms.en: hurry up, or else we will be late

sentence.da: Skynd dig, **ellers** kommer vi for sent.
sentence.en: Hurry up, or else we will be late.

elleve.explanation: "Elleve" means "eleven", the number 11. For the order word, say elvte (eleventh).

sentence.da: Et fodboldhold har **elleve** spillere.
sentence.en: A football team has eleven players.

elvte.explanation: "Elvte" means "eleventh" and gives a place in order, often in dates. The number itself is elleve (eleven).

sentence.da: Min fødselsdag er den **elvte** maj.
sentence.en: My birthday is May 11th.

empati.explanation: "Empati" means "empathy", the ability to feel and understand what someone else is going through. It is not the same as medlidenhed (pity): empati is about understanding the feeling, while medlidenhed is about feeling sorry for the person.

sentence.da: En læge med **empati** lytter og forstår, hvordan patienten har det.
sentence.en: A doctor with empathy listens and understands how the patient feels.

en e-mail.explanation: "En e-mail" means "an email". In daily speech, people often shorten it to en mail. You say at sende en e-mail (to send an email) and at modtage en e-mail (to receive an email).

sentence.da: En **e-mail** er et brev på computeren.
sentence.en: An email is a letter on the computer.

en edderkop.explanation: "En edderkop" means "a spider", a small animal with eight legs that often makes a web.

sentence.da: En **edderkop** spinder et net i hjørnet.
sentence.en: A spider spins a web in the corner.

en effekt.explanation: "En effekt" means "an effect", the result of something. Det har ingen effekt (It has no effect) is a common phrase when something does not work.

sentence.da: Musik har en god **effekt** på mig.
sentence.en: Music has a good effect on me.

en efterforsker.explanation: "En efterforsker" means "an investigator", a person whose job is to find out what happened in a crime or a case. The matching action is at efterforske (to investigate).

sentence.da: En **efterforsker** samler spor og taler med vidner.
sentence.en: An investigator collects clues and talks to witnesses.

en efterforskning.explanation: "En efterforskning" means "an investigation", the work of finding out the facts about a crime or an accident. The person doing it is en efterforsker.

sentence.da: Efter branden startede politiet en **efterforskning** af årsagen.
sentence.en: After the fire the police started an investigation of the cause.

en efterfølger.explanation: "En efterfølger" means "a successor", the person who takes over a job or position after someone. It is also used for a sequel: Filmen fik en efterfølger (The film got a sequel).

sentence.da: Direktøren går på pension, og hans **efterfølger** starter i morgen.
sentence.en: The director is retiring, and his successor starts tomorrow.

en efterløn.explanation: "En efterløn" means "an early-retirement pension", money that some Danes can get if they stop working a few years before the normal retirement age. People pay into a special fund to qualify, and the rules have become stricter over the years.

sentence.da: Hvis du går på **efterløn**, kan du stoppe med at arbejde før tid.
sentence.en: If you go on early retirement, you can stop working early.

en eftermiddag.explanation: "En eftermiddag" means "an afternoon", the part of the day from lunch until evening. Om eftermiddagen means "in the afternoon", and i eftermiddag means "this afternoon". The word is built from efter (after) and middag (midday).

sentence.da: Klokken fire er det **eftermiddag**.
sentence.en: It is afternoon at four o'clock.

en eftermiddagskaffe.explanation: "En eftermiddagskaffe" means "an afternoon coffee", a cup of coffee in the afternoon, often with something sweet.

sentence.da: Vi drikker **eftermiddagskaffe** klokken tre og spiser lidt kage.
sentence.en: We drink afternoon coffee at three o'clock and eat a little cake.

en efterskole.explanation: "En efterskole" means "a boarding school" for ages 14 to 18, a Danish kind of school that students choose instead of the last years of regular school. Many have a focus such as music, sport or art.

sentence.da: På en **efterskole** bor eleverne på skolen og har timer sammen.
sentence.en: At an efterskole the students live at the school and have lessons together.

en efterårsdag.explanation: "En efterårsdag" means "a fall day". It is built from efterår (fall) and dag (day). I efteråret means "in the fall".

sentence.da: Det er en kold **efterårsdag** i oktober.
sentence.en: It is a cold fall day in October.

en efterårsferie.explanation: "En efterårsferie" means "a fall break", a week off from school, usually in October.

sentence.da: Børnene har **efterårsferie** og er hjemme fra skole.
sentence.en: The children have fall break and are home from school.

en eg.explanation: "En eg" means "an oak", a big tree with very hard wood that is used for furniture and floors.

sentence.da: Under en **eg** ligger der mange agern om efteråret.
sentence.en: Under an oak there are many acorns in the autumn.

en egenskab.explanation: "En egenskab" means "a quality" or "a trait", something that is true of a person or a thing, like being kind or strong. It can be good or bad: en god egenskab, en dårlig egenskab (a good trait, a bad trait).

sentence.da: Tålmodighed er en vigtig **egenskab** hos en god lærer.
sentence.en: Patience is an important trait in a good teacher.

en ejendom.explanation: "En ejendom" means "a property", a building with its land, or the land alone. It is also the word for what you own in general: privat ejendom (private property).

sentence.da: Hun købte en gammel **ejendom** med tre lejligheder og en have.
sentence.en: She bought an old property with three apartments and a garden.

en ejendomsmægler.explanation: "En ejendomsmægler" means "a real estate agent", a person who helps owners sell their house or apartment, shows it to buyers and arranges the price. The ending -mægler means a go-between, as in en børsmægler (a stockbroker).

sentence.da: Vores **ejendomsmægler** viste huset frem for mange interesserede.
sentence.en: Our real estate agent showed the house to many interested people.

en ejer.explanation: "En ejer" means "an owner", the person something belongs to. It comes from at eje (to own).

sentence.da: Hunden kom hjem til sin **ejer**.
sentence.en: The dog came home to its owner.

en ejerbolig.explanation: "En ejerbolig" means "an owner-occupied home", a home that you own yourself, whether it is a house or an apartment, unlike a rented one.

sentence.da: Vi bor i vores egen **ejerbolig**, så vi betaler ikke husleje.
sentence.en: We live in our own home, so we do not pay rent.

en ejerlejlighed.explanation: "En ejerlejlighed" means "a condominium", an apartment that you own yourself, together with a share of the parts that everyone uses, such as the stairs and the roof.

sentence.da: Hun har købt en **ejerlejlighed** og deler gården med naboerne.
sentence.en: She has bought a condominium and shares the courtyard with the neighbors.

en eks.explanation: "En eks" means "an ex", a former boyfriend, girlfriend or partner. The longer form is en ekskæreste (an ex-boyfriend / ex-girlfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg så min **eks** i byen, men vi talte ikke.
sentence.en: I saw my ex in town, but we did not talk.

en eksamen.explanation: "En eksamen" means "an exam", the big test at the end of a course: Hun læser til eksamen (She is studying for her exam). It is a formal, graded test, not a quick quiz in class.

sentence.da: Jeg er nervøs, fordi jeg har **eksamen** i morgen.
sentence.en: I am nervous because I have an exam tomorrow.

en eksaminator.explanation: "En eksaminator" means "an examiner", the teacher who asks the questions at an oral exam. The outside person who listens and helps decide the grade is en censor (an external grader).

sentence.da: Min lærer var **eksaminator** ved den mundtlige eksamen.
sentence.en: My teacher was the examiner at the oral exam.

en eksistens.explanation: "En eksistens" means "an existence", the fact that something is real and is there. It can also mean a person: en tvivlsom eksistens (a shady character).

sentence.da: Børnene tror ikke længere på julemandens **eksistens**.
sentence.en: The children no longer believe in Santa's existence.

en ekskursion.explanation: "En ekskursion" means "a field trip", a planned trip with a purpose, usually organized by a school or a club to see or study something, such as a factory or a forest. An ordinary day out is en udflugt (an outing).

sentence.da: Klassen tager på **ekskursion** til et museum og ser dinosaurer.
sentence.en: The class goes on a field trip to a museum and sees dinosaurs.

en ekskæreste.explanation: "En ekskæreste" means "an ex", a former boyfriend or girlfriend. It is built from eks- (former) and en kæreste (a boyfriend or girlfriend). Kæreste does not say if the person is a man or a woman: min kæreste (my partner).

sentence.da: Jeg er stadig venner med min **ekskæreste**.
sentence.en: I am still friends with my ex.

en eksmand.explanation: "En eksmand" means "an ex-husband". It is built from eks- (former) and en mand (a man or husband). After min (my), mand means husband: min mand (my husband).

sentence.da: Hendes **eksmand** hentede børnene i går.
sentence.en: Her ex-husband picked up the children yesterday.

en ekspedient.explanation: "En ekspedient" means "a store clerk", the person who helps customers in a store. The word is the same for a man or a woman.

sentence.da: Jeg spørger en **ekspedient** om størrelsen.
sentence.en: I ask a store clerk about the size.

en ekspedition.explanation: "En ekspedition" means "a service" or "a transaction", the handling of one person or one case, for example at a counter in a shop or at a public office. It also means "an expedition", a long trip to explore a place: en ekspedition til Grønland (an expedition to Greenland).

related.en: to handle a person at a counter

sentence.da: I butikken tager hver **ekspedition** kun et minut.
sentence.en: In the shop, each transaction takes only a minute.

en ekspert.explanation: "En ekspert" means "an expert", someone who knows a lot about one subject. After er (is), en is often left out: Hun er ekspert i vin (She is an expert in wine).

sentence.da: Vi skal spørge en **ekspert** om hjælp.
sentence.en: We should ask an expert for help.

en eksplosion.explanation: "En eksplosion" means "an explosion", a sudden, very loud noise from something bursting. It can also describe a sudden jump: en eksplosion i priserne (a sudden jump in prices).

sentence.da: Vi hørte en stor **eksplosion** i nat.
sentence.en: We heard a big explosion last night.

en elastik.explanation: "En elastik" means "a rubber band", the stretchy loop that holds things together. It also means the elastic in clothes: Der er elastik i bukserne (There is elastic in the pants).

sentence.da: Jeg samler papirerne med en **elastik**.
sentence.en: I hold the papers together with a rubber band.

en elbil.explanation: "En elbil" means "an electric car". It is built from el (electricity) and bil (car), and el also starts en elcykel (an electric bike).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **elbil**, og den kører uden benzin.
sentence.en: I have an electric car, and it runs without gas.

en elefant.explanation: "En elefant" means "an elephant", the biggest land animal, gray and found in Africa and Asia.

sentence.da: En **elefant** har en lang snabel.
sentence.en: An elephant has a long trunk.

en elektriker.explanation: "En elektriker" means "an electrician", the person you call for wiring and lights.

sentence.da: Vi ringer til en **elektriker**, fordi lyset ikke virker.
sentence.en: We call an electrician because the light does not work.

en elektronikbutik.explanation: "En elektronikbutik" means "an electronics store", a place that sells computers, headphones and other devices. Big household machines like a washer are called hvidevarer (white goods).

sentence.da: I en **elektronikbutik** kan man købe fjernsyn, telefoner og høretelefoner.
sentence.en: In an electronics store you can buy TVs, phones and headphones.

en elev.explanation: "En elev" means "a pupil", a child or young person who goes to school. It can also mean a trainee at a workplace: Hun er elev hos en elektriker (She is a trainee with an electrician). Adults who study at university are usually called en studerende (a student) rather than elev.

sentence.da: Min søn er **elev** i tredje klasse.
sentence.en: My son is a pupil in third grade.

en elevator.explanation: "En elevator" means "an elevator". Danes also say en lift (a lift). You go up or down med elevatoren (by the elevator).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **elevator** op til femte sal.
sentence.en: We take an elevator up to the fifth floor.

en elg.explanation: "En elg" means "a moose" or "an elk", the same large animal with wide flat antlers. Americans call it a moose; the American elk is a different animal, called en wapiti in Danish.

sentence.da: En **elg** er verdens største hjort og har et bredt gevir.
sentence.en: A moose is the world's largest deer and has wide antlers.

en elkedel.explanation: "En elkedel" means "an electric kettle", used to heat water fast. It is built from el (electricity) and kedel (kettle), and el also starts en elbil (an electric car).

sentence.da: Jeg varmer vand til te i min **elkedel**.
sentence.en: I heat water for tea in my electric kettle.

en elpære.explanation: "En elpære" means "a light bulb". It is built from el (electricity) and pære (pear), because the bulb is shaped like one: Elpæren er sprunget (The light bulb has burned out).

sentence.da: Jeg skal købe en ny **elpære** til lampen.
sentence.en: I have to buy a new light bulb for the lamp.

en elregning.explanation: "En elregning" means "an electricity bill", the bill from the power company for what you use at home. It is built from el (electricity) and regning (bill). In a restaurant, you ask for the bill with Regningen, tak (The check, please).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler min **elregning** hver måned.
sentence.en: I pay my electricity bill every month.

en elskerinde.explanation: "En elskerinde" means "a mistress", a woman who has a secret love relationship with someone who is already with another person. The male version is en elsker (a lover).

sentence.da: Han havde en **elskerinde**, som hans kone ikke kendte til.
sentence.en: He had a mistress that his wife did not know about.

en embedsmand.explanation: "En embedsmand" means "a civil servant", a person who works for the state, for example in a government office. Embedsmænd (civil servants) usually keep their jobs when a new government comes in, unlike ministers.

sentence.da: En **embedsmand** forbereder lovene, og politikerne træffer beslutningen.
sentence.en: A civil servant prepares the laws, and the politicians make the decision.

en emhætte.explanation: "En emhætte" means "a range hood", the hood above a stove that pulls steam and smells out of the kitchen.

sentence.da: Der er en **emhætte** over komfuret.
sentence.en: There is a range hood over the stove.

en emission.explanation: "En emission" means "an emission", gas or particles sent out into the air, especially in talk about pollution and the environment. In finance it has another meaning: en emission af aktier (an issue of shares).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **emission** af gasser fra fabrikkens skorsten.
sentence.en: There is a large emission of gases from the factory's chimney.

en emoji.explanation: "En emoji" means "an emoji", the same word as in English. Danes add emojis to texts to show a feeling, like a smile or a heart.

sentence.da: En **emoji** er et lille billede i en besked.
sentence.en: An emoji is a small picture in a message.

en encyklopædi.explanation: "En encyklopædi" means "an encyclopedia", a big work with entries on many subjects in alphabetical order. Danes often use the shorter et leksikon (a lexicon) for the same thing.

sentence.da: I en **encyklopædi** kan man slå op, hvad en vulkan er.
sentence.en: In an encyclopedia you can look up what a volcano is.

en ende.explanation: "En ende" means "an end", the last part of something long, like a rope or a road. For the end of a story or an event, use en slutning (an ending).

sentence.da: Der er en café i den anden **ende** af gaden.
sentence.en: There is a cafe at the other end of the street.

en endelse.explanation: "En endelse" means "an ending", the letters at the end of a word that change its form. In talede (spoke), the endelse is -ede. For the end of a story, use en slutning (a conclusion).

sentence.da: Når man bøjer et ord, ændrer man ofte dets **endelse**.
sentence.en: When you change the form of a word, you often change its ending.

en endestation.explanation: "En endestation" means "a terminus", the last stop of a train or bus line. It is built from ende (end) and station (station). Ende also appears in i enden af gaden (at the end of the street).

sentence.da: Toget har **endestation** i Roskilde.
sentence.en: The train's last stop is Roskilde.

en energikilde.explanation: "En energikilde" means "an energy source", something that gives us power for heat, light and machines. It is built from energi (energy) and kilde (source). Kilde also means a water spring: en kilde i skoven (a spring in the forest).

sentence.da: Solen er en ren **energikilde**, og den er gratis.
sentence.en: The sun is a clean energy source, and it is free.

en eng.explanation: "En eng" means "a meadow", an open grassy place where wild flowers grow. Do not mix it up with en mark (a field), which is used for crops.

sentence.da: Der vokser vilde blomster på den grønne **eng**.
sentence.en: Wild flowers grow on the green meadow.

en engel.explanation: "En engel" means "an angel", a helper from heaven in stories. It is also used for a very kind person: Du er en engel! (You are an angel!).

sentence.da: Hun malede en **engel** med store vinger.
sentence.en: She painted an angel with big wings.

en englænder.explanation: "En englænder" means "an Englishman" or "an English person". The country is England, and the language is engelsk (English).

sentence.da: Han er **englænder**, men han taler godt dansk.
sentence.en: He is English, but he speaks good Danish.

en enhed.explanation: "En enhed" means "a device", a piece of equipment such as a laptop or a printer that connects to a network. It also means "a unit", for example a measure: En meter er en enhed for længde (A meter is a unit of length).

sentence.da: Telefonen er en **enhed**, som man kan koble til wifi.
sentence.en: The phone is a device that you can connect to wifi.

en enke.explanation: "En enke" means "a widow", a woman whose husband has died.

sentence.da: Hendes mand er død, og nu er hun **enke**.
sentence.en: Her husband has died, and now she is a widow.

en enkeltbillet.explanation: "En enkeltbillet" means "a one-way ticket". It is built from enkelt (single) and billet (ticket). The ticket for the trip back is en returbillet (a return ticket).

sentence.da: En **enkeltbillet** er kun til én tur.
sentence.en: A one-way ticket is only for one trip.

en enlig forsørger.explanation: "En enlig forsørger" means "a single parent", an adult who raises and pays for a child alone. The word en forsørger (a provider) puts the focus on paying for the family.

sentence.da: Som **enlig forsørger** skal hun både tjene penge og passe børnene.
sentence.en: As a single parent she must both earn money and look after the children.

en entré.explanation: "En entré" means "a hallway", the area just inside the front door. Entré also means an admission fee: Der er gratis entré (Admission is free).

sentence.da: Vi tager skoene af i vores **entré**.
sentence.en: We take our shoes off in our hallway.

en epidemi.explanation: "En epidemi" means "an epidemic", a sudden outbreak of an illness in one area. The worldwide version has a different word, so do not use epidemi for it.

sentence.da: En **epidemi** breder sig hurtigt og rammer mange mennesker.
sentence.en: An epidemic spreads quickly and hits many people.

en episode.explanation: "En episode" means "an episode", one part of a TV show or podcast. Et afsnit (an episode) means the same.

sentence.da: Jeg glæder mig til næste **episode** af podcasten.
sentence.en: I am looking forward to the next episode of the podcast.

en erfaring.explanation: "En erfaring" means "experience" you have gained from doing something. For something that happens to you, use en oplevelse (an experience).

sentence.da: Jeg har tre års **erfaring** som kok.
sentence.en: I have three years of experience as a cook.

en ergoterapeut.explanation: "En ergoterapeut" means "an occupational therapist", a health worker who helps people manage tasks like dressing and cooking after an injury or illness. A fysioterapeut (physical therapist) is the one who trains muscles and joints.

sentence.da: En **ergoterapeut** hjælper patienten med at klare hverdagen efter en skade.
sentence.en: An occupational therapist helps the patient manage daily life after an injury.

en erhvervsuddannelse.explanation: "En erhvervsuddannelse" means "a vocational education", training for a particular trade such as electrician, carpenter or chef. It is often shortened to EUD.

sentence.da: En **erhvervsuddannelse** består af skole og praktik hos en virksomhed.
sentence.en: A vocational education consists of school and a work placement at a company.

en erindring.explanation: "En erindring" means "a memory" of something in the past. The plural erindringer means "memoirs", the book a person writes about their own life: Han har skrevet sine erindringer (He has written his memoirs).

sentence.da: Pludselig dukkede en **erindring** fra barndommen op.
sentence.en: Suddenly a memory from childhood popped up.

en erkendelse.explanation: "En erkendelse" means "a realization", something you suddenly see clearly, often about yourself or life. It can also mean owning up to something: erkendelse af skyld (owning up to guilt).

sentence.da: Efter turen kom hun til en **erkendelse** af, hvad der er vigtigt.
sentence.en: After the trip, she came to a realization of what is important.

en erklæring.explanation: "En erklæring" means "a declaration" or "a statement", something said or signed officially to make a position or a fact clear. It also covers a signed paper, such as en erklæring om samtykke (a declaration of consent).

sentence.da: Politikeren afgav en **erklæring** om, at han ville stoppe.
sentence.en: The politician gave a statement saying that he would stop.

en erstatning.explanation: "En erstatning" means "compensation", money paid for damage or loss, and also "a replacement", a thing or person that takes the place of another. The sentence shows which meaning is used.

sentence.da: Forsikringen gav mig en **erstatning**, da cyklen blev stjålet.
sentence.en: The insurance gave me compensation when the bike was stolen.

en etage.explanation: "En etage" means "a floor", as a level of a building. The floor you walk on is et gulv (a floor).

sentence.da: Vi bor på tredje **etage** og tager trappen.
sentence.en: We live on the third floor and take the stairs.

en etagebolig.explanation: "En etagebolig" means "an apartment in a multi-story building". It is built from etage (floor) and bolig (home). Bolig is the general word for any place where you live, and it is linked to at bo (to live).

forms.en: an apartment in a multi-story building
the apartment in a multi-story building

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **etagebolig** midt i byen.
sentence.en: We live in an apartment in the middle of town.

en euro.explanation: "En euro" means "a euro", the money used in many European countries, such as France and Italy. Denmark has its own money, so Danish prices are not in euros.

sentence.da: I Frankrig betaler man med **euro**.
sentence.en: In France, people pay with euros.

en europæer.explanation: "En europæer" means "a European", a person from Europe. For things from Europe, use europæisk: europæisk historie (European history).

sentence.da: Som **europæer** kan jeg rejse frit i mange lande.
sentence.en: As a European, I can travel freely in many countries.

en evakuering.explanation: "En evakuering" means "an evacuation", moving people quickly out of a dangerous place, for example in a flood or a gas leak. The verb is at evakuere (to evacuate).

sentence.da: Under en **evakuering** forlader alle bygningen hurtigt og i ro.
sentence.en: During an evacuation, everyone leaves the building quickly and calmly.

en evighed.explanation: "En evighed" means "an eternity", time that never ends. In everyday speech it is also a very long time: Det varede en evighed (It took forever).

sentence.da: Nogle tror, at sjælen lever i **evighed**.
sentence.en: Some believe the soul lives for eternity.

en evne.explanation: "En evne" means "an ability", what someone is able to do or learn, often something you are born with. After it, use til (to): en evne til at lære (an ability to learn).

sentence.da: Hun har en stor **evne** til at lytte til andre.
sentence.en: She has a great ability to listen to others.

end.explanation: "End" means "than": Hun er højere end mig (She is taller than me). It comes after words like større (bigger) or bedre (better). Don't use som for "than". Som means "as": Han er lige så høj som mig (He is as tall as me).

sentence.da: En bil er hurtigere **end** en cykel.
sentence.en: A car is faster than a bicycle.

endda.explanation: "Endda" means "even" and adds something more surprising to what you just said: Han kan endda tale kinesisk (He can even speak Chinese).

sentence.da: Jeg har **endda** mødt kongen.
sentence.en: I have even met the king.

endelig.explanation: "Endelig" means "finally" or "at last": Endelig! (At last!). It also makes an invitation warmer: Tag endelig en kage (Please do take a cake).

forms.en: Be sure not to forget to call.

sentence.da: **Endelig** er det weekend, og vi har fri.
sentence.en: Finally, it is the weekend, and we are off.

endeligt.explanation: "Endeligt" means "definitively", for good, with no more changes. Do not mix it up with endelig (finally): Endelig! (At last!)

sentence.da: Beslutningen er **endeligt** truffet, og den kan ikke ændres.
sentence.en: The decision is definitively made, and it cannot be changed.

endnu.explanation: "Endnu" means "yet" or "still". Ikke endnu means "not yet": Har du spist? Nej, ikke endnu (Have you eaten? No, not yet). With en it means "another": endnu en kop kaffe (another cup of coffee). Before a word like bedre it means "even": endnu bedre (even better).

sentence.da: Jeg er ikke færdig **endnu**.
sentence.en: I am not finished yet.

endskønt.explanation: "Endskønt" means "although" and starts a part of a sentence, like the everyday selvom (in spite of the fact that). It is more formal, so you meet it mostly in books and speeches, while people say selvom when they talk.

forms.da: endskønt vi var sent på den

sentence.da: **Endskønt** det regnede, gik vi en lang tur.
sentence.en: Although it rained, we went on a long walk.

endvidere.explanation: "Endvidere" means "furthermore" and adds one more point to what you just said. It sounds formal, so you find it mostly in letters, reports and speeches; in everyday talk Danes say og så (and also).

sentence.da: Bilen er billig, og **endvidere** bruger den meget lidt benzin.
sentence.en: The car is cheap, and furthermore it uses very little gas.

energi.explanation: "Energi" means "energy", both power that makes things run and the strength you feel: Jeg har ikke energi i dag (I have no energy today). Power from the wall is called strøm (electricity).

sentence.da: Vindmøller laver **energi** af vinden.
sentence.en: Wind turbines make energy from the wind.

energisk.explanation: "Energisk" means "energetic" and describes someone full of energy: Han er energisk om morgenen (He is energetic in the morning). The opposite is sløv (sluggish).

sentence.da: Han er **energisk** og løber hver morgen.
sentence.en: He is energetic and runs every morning.

eneste.explanation: "Eneste" means "only" or "single", as in the only one. It normally comes after den, det or de (the): den eneste for en-words, det eneste for et-words. Do not mix it up with kun (just, only): Jeg har kun én bil (I have only one car).

sentence.da: Han er den **eneste** læge her.
sentence.en: He is the only doctor here.

enestående.explanation: "Enestående" means "unique" or "outstanding". It is built from ene (alone) and stående (standing), so it describes something that stands by itself with nothing like it. It is positive, used for praise, not for something merely odd.

sentence.da: Hun er helt **enestående**, for der er ingen som hende.
sentence.en: She is completely unique, because there is nobody like her.

engang.explanation: "Engang" (one word) means "once" or "some day", for a time you do not name exactly: Der var engang... (Once upon a time...), Kom og besøg mig engang (Come and visit me sometime). En gang (two words) means "one time": en gang om dagen (once a day).

forms.en: Come and visit me some day!

sentence.da: Jeg boede i Italien **engang**.
sentence.en: I once lived in Italy.

engelsk.explanation: "Engelsk" means "English", for the language and for things from England. As a school subject, say Jeg har engelsk (I have English, meaning an English lesson). Words for languages start with a small letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Hun er fra England og taler **engelsk**.
sentence.en: She is from England and speaks English.

england.explanation: "England" means "England". It is only one part of the United Kingdom; for Great Britain as a whole, say Storbritannien (Great Britain).

sentence.da: London er en stor by i **England**.
sentence.en: London is a big city in England.

enhver.explanation: "Enhver" means "anyone" or "every", and stresses that it holds for each person: Enhver har ret til en pause (Everyone has the right to a break). With an et-word, it becomes ethvert.

sentence.da: **Enhver** kan lære at svømme.
sentence.en: Anyone can learn to swim.

enig.explanation: "Enig" means "in agreement". Danes say it with er (am/is/are): Jeg er enig (I agree), Det er jeg enig i (I agree with that).

sentence.da: Jeg er helt **enig** med dig om det her.
sentence.en: I completely agree with you about this.

enig med.explanation: "Enig med" means "in agreement with" a person: Jeg er enig med min mor (I agree with my mom). For an idea or opinion, use enig i: Jeg er enig i det (I agree with that).

forms.da: Vi er ikke enige med ham.
forms.en: We do not agree with him.

sentence.da: Jeg er helt **enig med** dig.
sentence.en: I completely agree with you.

enkel.explanation: "Enkel" means "simple" in the sense of plain and not complicated: Opskriften er enkel (The recipe is simple). For easy to do, use let (easy).

sentence.da: Reglen er **enkel**, så alle kan lære den.
sentence.en: The rule is simple, so everyone can learn it.

enkelt.explanation: "Enkelt" means "single" or "simple". En enkelt person (a single person) is just one, and Det er enkelt (It is simple) means it is easy.

sentence.da: Svaret er helt **enkelt**.
sentence.en: The answer is quite simple.

enkeltvis.explanation: "Enkeltvis" means "one by one", dealing with things separately rather than together. It is built from enkelt (single) and -vis (in the way of), the same ending as in parvis (in pairs).

sentence.da: Patienterne bliver kaldt ind **enkeltvis**, ikke i grupper.
sentence.en: The patients are called in one by one, not in groups.

enlig.explanation: "Enlig" means "single" or "solitary". It describes someone without a partner, as in en enlig mor (a single mother), or something standing by itself. To say you are not in a relationship, Danes usually say Jeg er single (I am single).

sentence.da: Hun er **enlig** og opdrager sine to børn alene.
sentence.en: She is a single parent and raises her two children alone.

enogtyve.explanation: "Enogtyve" means "twenty-one". Danish says the one first: en-og-tyve is literally one-and-twenty. The same goes for 22, toogtyve (two-and-twenty), and 31, enogtredive (one-and-thirty).

sentence.da: Min søn er **enogtyve** år.
sentence.en: My son is twenty-one years old.

enorm.explanation: "Enorm" means "enormous", far bigger than normal: Hvalen er enorm (The whale is enormous).

sentence.da: Elefanten er **enorm** og vejer mange tons.
sentence.en: The elephant is enormous and weighs many tons.

enormt.explanation: "Enormt" means "enormously" and makes the next word much stronger: Det er enormt dyrt (It is enormously expensive).

sentence.da: Den film var **enormt** sjov.
sentence.en: That movie was hugely funny.

ens.explanation: "Ens" means "identical" or "alike" and says that things are the same: De to søstre er ens (The two sisters are alike). You need two or more things to compare.

sentence.da: De to huse er helt **ens**.
sentence.en: The two houses are exactly alike.

ensfarvet.explanation: "Ensfarvet" means "solid-colored", all in one color with no pattern. It is built from ens (the same) and farvet (colored), and you use it for clothes, fabric and walls.

sentence.da: Tøjet er **ensfarvet**, så der er hverken striber eller prikker.
sentence.en: The clothes are solid-colored, so there are neither stripes nor dots.

ensomhed.explanation: "Ensomhed" means "loneliness", the feeling of being alone even when people are around: Mange ældre kender ensomhed (Many older people know loneliness). Someone who feels it is ensom (lonely): Jeg føler mig ensom (I feel lonely).

sentence.da: Efter flytningen følte hun **ensomhed**, men hun fandt venner.
sentence.en: After the move she felt loneliness, but she found friends.

ental.explanation: "Et ental" means "singular", the word form for just one thing: en bog (a book) is ental, but bøger (books) is not. You hear it in grammar class, when you are asked to put a word i ental (in the singular).

sentence.da: Ordet bil er i **ental**, fordi det kun handler om én bil.
sentence.en: The word bil (car) is in the singular because it is only about one car.

enten.explanation: "Enten" means "either" and works with eller (or) to give two choices: Vi tager enten bussen eller toget (We take either the bus or the train). Together, enten ... eller means "either ... or".

forms.da: enten i dag eller i morgen

sentence.da: Du kan **enten** betale kontant eller med kort.
sentence.en: You can pay either in cash or by card.

enten…eller.explanation: "Enten … eller" means "either … or" and gives two choices: Enten i dag eller i morgen (Either today or tomorrow). Enten goes before the first choice and "eller" before the second. For "neither … nor", say hverken … eller: Jeg vil hverken have kaffe eller te (I want neither coffee nor tea).

forms.da: Enten i dag eller i morgen.
Enten er du med, eller også er du ikke.
forms.en: Either you are in, or you are not.

sentence.da: Vi kan **enten** gå **eller** tage bussen.
sentence.en: We can either walk or take the bus.

entusiastisk.explanation: "Entusiastisk" means "enthusiastic", showing strong, happy interest in something. It describes both people and their reactions, as in en entusiastisk modtagelse (an enthusiastic reception). The person who feels it is en entusiast (an enthusiast).

sentence.da: Hun er altid **entusiastisk**, når hun taler om sit arbejde.
sentence.en: She is always enthusiastic when she talks about her work.

er det ...?.explanation: "Er det ...?" means "is it ...?". Danish asks a question by putting er (is) first, with no extra word like do: Er det rigtigt? (Is that right?). Fill the gap with whatever you want to ask about.

sentence.da: **Er det** langt herfra?
sentence.en: Is it far from here?

er du sikker?.explanation: "Er du sikker?" means "are you sure?". Sikker means "sure", and also "safe": en sikker bil (a safe car). To ask several people, say Er I sikre? (Are you all sure?).

sentence.da: **Er du sikker?** Det er en lang tur.
sentence.en: Are you sure? It is a long trip.

erfaren.explanation: "Erfaren" means "experienced", about a person who knows a job well after doing it for a long time. It matches en erfaring (experience gained by doing), not en oplevelse (something you go through, like a trip).

sentence.da: Han er en **erfaren** pilot og har fløjet i tyve år.
sentence.en: He is an experienced pilot and has flown for twenty years.

et efternavn.explanation: "Et efternavn" means "a last name", the family name you share with your family. It is made of efter (after) and et navn (a name). Efter (after) also starts et efterår (an autumn).

sentence.da: Mit **efternavn** er Hansen.
sentence.en: My last name is Hansen.

et efterår.explanation: "Et efterår" means "an autumn" (or "a fall" in American English), the season between summer and winter. It is made of efter (after) and et år (a year). Efter (after) also starts et efternavn (a last name).

sentence.da: Det er **efterår** med mange røde blade.
sentence.en: It is fall, with many red leaves.

et egern.explanation: "Et egern" means "a squirrel", a small animal with a long bushy tail.

sentence.da: Et **egern** gemmer nødder til vinteren.
sentence.en: A squirrel hides nuts for the winter.

et ego.explanation: "Et ego" means "an ego", your sense of who you are and how important you feel. When someone is full of themselves, Danes say Han har et stort ego (He has a big ego).

sentence.da: Hendes **ego** blev såret, da ingen ville høre hendes mening.
sentence.en: Her ego was hurt when nobody wanted to hear her opinion.

et ekko.explanation: "Et ekko" means "an echo", a sound that comes back.

sentence.da: I bjergene kan man høre et **ekko**.
sentence.en: In the mountains you can hear an echo.

et eksamensbevis.explanation: "Et eksamensbevis" means "a diploma", an official paper given by a school or university to show you passed your final tests. Employers often ask for it when you apply for a job.

sentence.da: Jeg sender mit **eksamensbevis** sammen med min ansøgning.
sentence.en: I am sending my diploma together with my application.

et eksempel.explanation: "Et eksempel" means "an example". For example is til eksempel, short t.eks., or for eksempel, short f.eks.

sentence.da: Kan du give et **eksempel**?
sentence.en: Can you give an example?

et eksperiment.explanation: "Et eksperiment" means "an experiment", a test to find something out. The matching verb is at eksperimentere (to experiment).

sentence.da: Børnene laver et **eksperiment** med vand.
sentence.en: The children do an experiment with water.

et emne.explanation: "Et emne" means "a subject" or "a topic" to talk or write about. For a school subject like math or history, use et fag (a school subject) instead.

sentence.da: Hvilket **emne** skal vi tale om?
sentence.en: Which topic should we talk about?

et enkeltværelse.explanation: "Et enkeltværelse" means "a single room", a hotel room for one person. It is made of enkelt (single) and et værelse (a room).

sentence.da: Jeg rejser alene og vil have et **enkeltværelse**.
sentence.en: I travel alone and want a single room.

et erhverv.explanation: "Et erhverv" means "a profession", the kind of work a person does to earn a living. It also names business in general, as in erhvervslivet (the business world).

sentence.da: Hendes **erhverv** er sygeplejerske, og hun arbejder på et hospital.
sentence.en: Her profession is nurse, and she works at a hospital.

et escape room.explanation: "Et escape room" means "an escape room", a game where a group is locked in a room and solves puzzles to get out. Danes use the English words.

sentence.da: Vi løste alle opgaverne i vores **escape room** og kom ud.
sentence.en: We solved all the tasks in our escape room and got out.

et essay.explanation: "Et essay" means "an essay", a piece of writing where the author explores a subject and gives personal views. It is freer and more personal than a school composition (en stil).

sentence.da: I sit **essay** skriver hun om, hvorfor vi har brug for stilhed.
sentence.en: In her essay, she writes about why we need silence.

et eventyr.explanation: "Et eventyr" means both "a fairy tale" and "an adventure". A fairy tale is an old made-up story, and an adventure is an exciting trip or experience: Rejsen var et eventyr (The trip was an adventure).

sentence.da: Der er en heks og en prins i dette **eventyr**.
sentence.en: There is a witch and a prince in this fairy tale.

ethvert.explanation: "Ethvert" means "every" and "any", stressing each one on its own. It goes before an et-word. With an en-word, use enhver: enhver mand (every man).

sentence.da: **Ethvert** barn har ret til at gå i skole.
sentence.en: Every child has a right to go to school.

etik.explanation: "Etik" means "ethics", thinking about what is right and wrong. It is also the rules a group follows in its work. The matching describing word is etisk (ethical): Det er ikke etisk (That is not ethical).

sentence.da: Lægernes **etik** siger, at patientens sikkerhed kommer først.
sentence.en: Doctors' ethics say that the patient's safety comes first.

eu.explanation: "EU" means "the EU", the group of European countries that work together. Danish says i EU (in the EU) with no word for "the".

sentence.da: Vi må arbejde i alle lande i **EU**.
sentence.en: We may work in all the countries in the EU.

europa.explanation: "Europa" means "Europe", the continent that includes Denmark, Germany and France.

sentence.da: Danmark ligger i **Europa**.
sentence.en: Denmark is in Europe.

europæisk.explanation: "Europæisk" means "European", for things that belong to Europe. Unlike English, it is written with a small letter: europæisk mad (European food).

sentence.da: Danmark er et **europæisk** land.
sentence.en: Denmark is a European country.

eventuel.explanation: "Eventuel" means "possible" and "any", for something that may or may not happen: Ring, hvis der er eventuelle problemer (Call if there are any problems). It does not mean what English eventual means (happening in the end). For that, use til sidst (in the end).

sentence.da: Hvis der er en **eventuel** fejl, skal du sige det.
sentence.en: If there is a possible error, you should say so.

evig.explanation: "Evig" means "eternal", lasting forever. It also fits things that never seem to end: en evig diskussion (a never-ending discussion).

sentence.da: De lovede hinanden **evig** kærlighed ved brylluppet.
sentence.en: They promised each other eternal love at the wedding.

evigt.explanation: "Evigt" means "forever" and says how long an action lasts: Jeg husker det evigt (I will remember it forever). Before a thing, Danish usually uses evig: evig kærlighed (eternal love).

sentence.da: Det varer **evigt**, når man venter på bussen.
sentence.en: It lasts forever when you wait for the bus.
